gen-dafont-starborn-gf-blinker: Blinker keeps every line at a steady thickness, with open curves and a lowercase that fills its height. Blinker's plain sans manner makes Starborn's wide gaps and dark lowercase stripe feel dreamier, and if the heading shrinks, those gaps may fall apart.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-carrois-gothic: Dreamy and spaced out, with a dark band of lowercase running through each line. And Carrois Gothic, a plain sans with a high x-height and generous c openings, gives Starborn a modern footing.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-carrois-gothic-sc: Starborn scatters its letters across wide gaps of blank space. Starborn is best at drifting, ethereal headings with a dark lowercase stripe, while Carrois Gothic SC, a sans-serif, keeps curves clearly open and capitals close to lowercase height.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-chivo: Starborn spreads its letters through wide blank gaps, with a thick, dark stripe of lowercase running through each line. Chivo, a sans-serif, packs its lowercase up toward the caps and keeps its curves visibly open.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-chocolate-classic: Dreamy, ethereal Starborn leaves big gaps between its letters and lays down a dark lowercase stripe. But Chocolate Classical Sans, a plain sans with a sizable lowercase and a broad-nibbed stroke that never curls shut, brings the modern, professional footing.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-comme: Comme reads smoothly, with no clogged curves and lowercase bodies that fill most of the letter height. Starborn does the dreamy work with wide gaps and a dark lowercase stripe, while Comme, a sans-serif, does the modern job of making each line go down easily.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-cossette-texte: Cossette Texte reads clean, with wide-eyed e shapes and a prominent x-height. Starborn is best at dreamy, wire-bent headings with wide gaps and a dark lowercase band, whereas Cossette Texte, a sans-serif, is best at plain, thick-arched text.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-duru-sans: Starborn's lowercase forms a thick, dark stripe, floating in wide gaps of blank space. Duru Sans, a sans with wide openings on small letters and ascenders that hardly show, lets bodies dominate the line, so a long stretch reads modern and clean.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-fresca: Starborn's wide blank gaps and dark lowercase stripe feel ethereal and low in stress. And Fresca, a sans with no calligraphic thinning and curves as heavy as cord, keeps counters open to the outside, so a long stretch reads clean.
gen-dafont-starborn-gf-funnel-sans: Starborn is the dreamy one, putting big gaps between its letters and a dark lowercase stripe through each line. Funnel Sans, a sans-serif, keeps its stroke widths constant, with tiny gaps below the ascender tops and an open e, so a long passage reads professional and clean.
